newsitem.title: USA: GM says minivan production on schedule.
newsitem.headline: GM says minivan production on schedule.

text.p: Production schedules for General Motors Corp's new minivans are accelerating according to plan at the automaker's Doraville, Ga., manufacturing facility, an executive said Thursday.
Fred Schaafsma, GM's vehicle line executive for minivans, said full capacity will be reached in 1997, although he declined to say specifically when, or what that capacity is.

Schaafsma said GM expects the U.S. minivan market to grow at three percent a year. GM expects to sell all of the new minivans it can make, he said, adding the firm's per-vehicle profit will be higher than on previous minivan versions.
Schaafsma's comments came as part of a lunch sponsored by the Automotive Press Association.

The new minivan launch is a particuarly complex one, he said, because of the number of models and variations GM is building at the single plant. "We're not going to declare victory until we're all done," he said.
About 15 percent of annual production will be shipped overseas. In addition to European versions, GM is introducing the Chevrolet Venture, Pontiac Trans Sport and Oldsmobile Silhouette minivans.
